objective: Earn qualified visits from readers of Classical Chinese and Chinese history by showing a real multilingual edition before asking for attention.

source_evidence.edition_format: 文言文 main text with English, modern Japanese, and modern Chinese

x.content: Reading 資治通鑑 in the original shouldn't mean losing the thread. I built a free public edition with 文言文 + English + modern Japanese + modern Chinese, in color and B&W. Search “LinguaLeaf” on GitHub to read it.
x.link_strategy: Postiz strips links from X drafts as of 2026-08-31; use direct visible X composition for a clickable canonical shelf URL after review.

instagram.content:
Some books are difficult because the language is distant—not because the ideas are.

I’ve been building a reading shelf for Chinese classics where 文言文 sits beside English, modern Japanese, and modern Chinese. It includes multilingual editions of 資治通鑑, 漢書, 後漢書, 三國志裴松之注, and 春秋左氏傳, in color and black-and-white formats.

Made with PocketPolyglot; the finished books live in the public LinguaLeaf shelf:
https://lachlanchen.github.io/LinguaLeaf/website/?utm_source=instagram&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=wenyan_history

Which history would you open first?
